anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Composite definition: The database is simultaneously affected by (1) stale or incomplete optimizer statistics that drive systematic cardinality misestimation, (2) heavy lock-manager blocking/deadlock situations among concurrent transactions, and (3) exhaustion or slowdown of network/connection-handling resources between clients and the server.
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly: Inaccurate or missing statistics misguide the cost-based optimizer, producing sub-optimal access paths and join orders.
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly: Incompatible lock requests from concurrent transactions create long blocking chains or deadlocks, throttling throughput.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly: Limited or unstable network, listener, socket, or authentication capacity delays session establishment and enlarges result-set transfer times.

Combined phenomena: Affected systems exhibit erratic query plans with unexpectedly large scans that lock many rows or pages, quickly generating extensive blocker–waiter trees. As blocked sessions pile up, client threads remain connected but idle, inflating session counts until the listener or socket backlog is saturated. Users observe a mixture of symptoms—slow or timed-out connections, sudden surges in lock wait time, deadlock error bursts, intermittent plan regressions after data loads, and highly variable response times—making root-cause isolation difficult.

Causal interaction: Misestimated cardinalities can cause the optimizer to choose plans that touch far more data than necessary (e.g., full table scans instead of index seeks), increasing the number, scope, and lifetime of locks held by each statement. The enlarged lock footprint heightens the probability and duration of lock contention and deadlocks. Prolonged blocking slows statement completion, so application sessions stay active longer, which in turn drives up the number of concurrent connections competing for limited listener threads, socket buffers, and network bandwidth. Conversely, network or authentication slowdowns extend transaction round-trip times, delaying commit/rollback and keeping locks in place even longer, thereby intensifying contention. The feedback loop between poor plans, prolonged locks, and network saturation can quickly degrade overall OLTP throughput and stability.

entry.official_definition: The length of time in seconds an InnoDB transaction waits for a row lock before giving up.
entry.trigger_condition: An InnoDB transaction waits longer than innodb_lock_wait_timeout for a row lock.
entry.workload_impact: The lock wait gives up; by default only the current statement is rolled back unless innodb_rollback_on_timeout is enabled.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as an InnoDB system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
